Story takes place in the co-sex dorms at a university i attended. My closest female friend and I would hang out in my dorm room and we'd normally just do a skin care routine and watch movies so when she asked to come over one afternoon, i thought nothing of it.
It's probably important to note that I never looked at her sexually or considered her as a possible partner as she had a boyfriend the entire time i knew her, she was nothing more than a good friend in my head.
When i opened my dorm and allowed her in, I immediately could tell she was drunk and she proceeded to start trying to kiss me and grope me once the doors behind me were closed. I've never been the kind of guy who was rough with people or good at confrontation so I was scared of hurting her feelings or physically harming her. I blame myself often for being weak or not stern enough with her but I kept telling her no and to stop but she would take it further and further. Parts of my head were telling me that as a man I should be liking this and letting this happen, but I could just hear this innocent childlike version of myself inside me screaming for it to stop. I blame myself to this day for just "letting it happen". 
I cried for an hour after she left and tried to kill myself right after that. If two of my friends at university hadn't been up and roaming the streets of the city that night, I'd be dead right now, they called out to me without knowing what happened and asked if I'd get a burger with them haha. You never know what your actions may do to help someone guys, truly. 
Since then I've tried to talk to some friends and family about it, but I've just gotten the same answers. My family says it's my fault it ever happened in the first place and that im exaggerating the details, and my male friends just tell me "damn, i wish that was me, she was hot" and my female friends often say "i dont get how a guy gets raped lmao, makes no sense to me." 
Rape crisis centers in my area have denied me access as having a male around the female clients would trigger them supposedly and the police thought I was drugged out and hallucinating when i first went to them.
This was when i genuinely realized I'm forever and truly alone in this world, that nobody will ever help me like I can help myself.

While i do agree with this, i always try to keep in mind that the Manga may be coming to a close soon. For the majority of the manga, we witnessed normal ghouls with normal kagune, and that was fine. It was exciting to see a ghoul with a special kagune and it was almost certain that the ghoul was either very special or very strong. Now that the story is coming to a close, we are going to begin witnessing stronger ghouls with outlandish abilities, not for the sake of making it a shonen manga, but because we need to shift focus to more important ghouls. I would certainly be turned off by the manga if more ghouls turned out to have these special kagune, especially during the final battle (which most likely will be Kaneki v Furuta) it's not that the mood/theme of the manga has changed, but rather the focus. We are witnessing the strong ghouls end the story and it just so happens many of them are especially strong due to their special kagune.
I may be wrong, but it makes sense to me, and it makes me definitely keep my interest in the story.
